newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open weaker with U.S. treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open weaker with U.S. treasuries.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened weaker on Tuesday, softening with U.S. treasuries as concern about supply being introduced in both markets this week weighed on prices, analysts said.
"Canada is following the U.S.," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed-income research with Midland Walwyn Capital Inc. "There's just a multitude of factors. Technicals have turned bearish."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.65 to C$110.50 to yield 7.108 percent. The U.S. 30-year bond fell 13/32 to yield 7.02 percent.
The spread between the bonds widened to nine basis points from seven basis points at the close of trading on Monday.

"We gave a good shot at getting that long Canada-U.S. spread below zero last week but couldn't make it," said Dong. "I think most people probably believe that it's going to take another really big effort to get that spread below zero. It probably won't be happening anytime soon."
Canadian bonds opened weaker with U.S. Treasuries as traders there were seen squaring positions ahead of this week's economic reports and two- and five-year bond auctions on Wednesday and Thursday.

Dong said that in Canada, traders are also positioning themselves ahead of tomorrow's five-year auction. The Government of Canada will auction C$2.6 billion of 5.5 percent bond due September 1, 2002. The Bank of Canada will acquire at least C$390 million of the new bonds.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.45 to C$102.90 to yield 6.585 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 6/32 to yield 6.77 percent.
The negative spread between the two bonds narrowed to 19 basis points from 23 basis points at the close of trading on Monday.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.91 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.17 percent.
